Hearty Beef and Root Vegetable Pie

Served at: St. Stephen's Day (Boxing Day)

Serves 6Prep 30 minCook 2 hr 30 min

Hearty Pie is a traditional dish served on St. Stephen's Day, also known as Boxing Day, in many Irish and British households. This comforting pie combines tender beef and root vegetables in a rich gravy, symbolizing warmth and togetherness during the winter holiday season.

Ingredients

  • 2 lbs (900 g) beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
  • 2 tbsp (30 ml) vegetable oil
  • 1 large onion, chopped
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 3 carrots, peeled and chopped
  • 2 parsnips, peeled and chopped
  • 2 celery stalks, chopped
  • 1 cup (240 ml) beef broth
  • 1 cup (240 ml) stout beer or dark ale
  • 2 tbsp (15 g) tomato paste
  • 2 tsp (4 g) Worcestershire sauce
  • 1 tsp (2 g) dried thyme
  • 1 tsp (2 g) dried rosemary
  • Salt and black pepper to taste
  • 2 tbsp (16 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 sheet frozen puff pastry, thawed
  • 1 egg, beaten (for egg wash)

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
  2. Heat vegetable oil in a large ovenproof pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
  3. Brown the beef cubes in batches until all sides are seared; remove and set aside.
  4. In the same pot, add onion and garlic; sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
  5. Add carrots, parsnips, and celery; cook for another 5 minutes.
  6. Return the beef to the pot and sprinkle flour over the mixture; stir well to coat.
  7. Add beef broth, stout beer, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper; stir to combine.
  8. Bring to a simmer, then cover and transfer the pot to the oven.
  9. Cook for 2 hours until beef is tender and sauce has thickened.
  10. Remove the pot from the oven and increase oven temperature to 400°F (200°C).
  11. Roll out the puff pastry to fit the top of the pot or transfer the filling to a pie dish and cover with pastry.
  12. Brush the pastry with beaten egg to give a golden finish.
  13. Bake uncovered for 25-30 minutes until the pastry is puffed and golden brown.
  14. Let the pie rest for 10 minutes before serving.

Tips

  • For a vegetarian version, substitute beef with mushrooms and use vegetable broth.
  • Adding a splash of red wine instead of stout can deepen the flavor.
  • Serve with mashed potatoes or steamed greens for a complete Boxing Day meal.
